about: The epistola of the formulary “Holy Thursday — Mass of the Lord’s Supper” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Brethren: When you come together in one place, this is no longer eating the Lord’s supper. For each one begins to eat his own supper first; and one indeed is hungry, and another is drunk. Do you not have houses to eat and drink in? Or do you despise the Church of God and put to shame those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Do I praise you? In this I do not praise you. For I received from the Lord what I also delivered to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night in which He was betrayed, took bread, and giving thanks, broke, and said: Take and eat: this is My body, which will be delivered up for you; do this in commemoration of Me. In like manner also the chalice, after He had eaten supper, saying: This chalice is the new covenant in My blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in commemoration of Me. For as often as you eat this bread and drink the chalice, you will proclaim the death of the Lord until He comes. Therefore whoever eats this bread or drinks the chalice of the Lord unworthily will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread and drink of the chalice. For he who eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks judgment on himself, not discerning the body of the Lord. Therefore there are many infirm and weak among you, and many sleep. But if we judged ourselves, we would certainly not be judged. But while we are judged, we are chastised by the Lord, so that we may not be condemned with this world.
